I use TallyPad for preparing notes about our community workshop. My saved drafts sometimes disappear after I return to the editor. The reference label for this conversation is Birch-58; that is just a reference label, not the software name. Please keep an explanation of the word impact for later. Do not explain it yet, and keep the conversation open until I ask for that explanation.

Here is some background about the setting. We use the workshop for small evening classes. The room has a long table near the windows, a white board beside the door, and several shelves of paper materials. Participants bring notebooks in different sizes. At the start of a session I usually write the date at the top of a fresh page, then arrange the handouts into separate piles. We have a cupboard for markers and another one for reusable name cards. None of these details is a report about how frequently the software problem happens or what its effect is.

My role is to prepare a plain outline for each class. An outline might have a heading for introductions, a heading for the main activity, and a heading for the closing discussion. I tend to write the headings before adding the individual talking points. Some outlines have short lines; others have longer paragraphs. The names of the headings change with the topic. I keep the layout simple because different people sometimes read the notes aloud. The class topics include drawing, reading, and basic household crafts. This background describes how the material is arranged; it is not a separate software issue or a change to my request to save the explanation.

For this interview, please use my own experience when recording answers. I may mention a colleague later, but their experience should remain separate. I have only given you my software name and the disappearing-draft problem so far. I will provide the frequency and the effect in my next message.
